findings.section: The three Directory Service options differ in where the directory runs (table, Exam signal, Stop and answer)
findings.quote: | Amazon RDS for SQL Server | Yes: [compatible with AWS Managed Microsoft AD only](../facts/directory-service.md#directory-service-rds-needs-managed-ad) | No |
findings.evidence: source_id docs/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_SQLServer_SelfManagedActiveDirectory (saved 2026-10-13): "Amazon RDS for SQL Server seamlessly integrates with your self-managed Active Directory (AD) domain, regardless of where your AD is hosted - whether in your data center, on Amazon EC2, or with other cloud providers. This integration enables direct user authentication through NTLM or Kerberos protocols, eliminating the need for complex intermediary domains or forest trusts." The fact directory-service-rds-needs-managed-ad quotes the AD Connector compatibility page ('compatible with AWS Managed Microsoft AD only'); read alone it tells her that RDS for SQL Server can never use the company's own AD. The same 'only' drives the Exam signal ('RDS for SQL Server with Windows Authentication points to AWS Managed Microsoft AD') and the Stop and answer ('What do you add ... AWS Managed Microsoft AD with a trust'). She works at AWS and will repeat this to founders. Fix: scope the claim to Directory Service: 'Of the Directory Service options, RDS works with AWS Managed Microsoft AD, not with AD Connector.' Add one Go deeper line (with a new fact request from the RDS page) that RDS for SQL Server can also join a self-managed AD directly. Keep Managed AD as the exam answer when the stem says 'managed' or 'least operational overhead'.
findings.resolution: Scoped to Directory Service: the table row is 'Yes, with [either a one-way or two-way trust]' | 'No: [not compatible with RDS SQL Server]'; the Exam signal says 'points to AWS Managed Microsoft AD, not AD Connector'; the Stop and answer asks 'Can AD Connector serve the database?'. The 'only' link is gone. The Go deeper line on RDS joining a self-managed AD needs a new fact; a fact request would stay open at finalize (B09), so it is listed for the registrar (claims-002).

findings.section: identity-federation-s01 (sixty_second, first line)
findings.quote: "Both sign people in, but they open different doors."
findings.evidence: Rule RULINGS hard rule 8 ('no idioms') and STYLE plain English. 'open different doors' is a metaphor that she must translate under stress, and the next line says the plain version ('The difference is who signs in'). Fix: 'Both sign people in, but into different places: your AWS accounts, or your app.' This also fixes the split of reader-05.
findings.resolution: s01 line 1: 'Both sign people in, but to different places: your AWS accounts, or your app.'; skeleton 'both sign in, different places'.

findings.section: Numbers that decide answers (A-list, row '1 hour')
findings.quote: | [1 hour] | Default permission set session; maximum [12 hours] | An account session outlasts a removed assignment |
findings.evidence: Fact iam-identity-center-role-sessions-persist-up-to-12-hours: "They persist for the duration configured in the permission set ... which can be up to 12 hours, regardless of the status of the original sign-in session." The 'Why it decides' cell states a result without the cause (the role session runs on its own once it starts), and says 'removed assignment' while the fact speaks of the sign-in session. Fix: 'An open role session runs to its end, even after sign-out: a longer session means slower revocation.'
findings.resolution: Why-it-decides cell now reads 'Role sessions outlive sign-out'.

findings.section: Question 9 (identity-federation-q012), Why not, option 3; shown in 5-quiz.md
findings.quote: A user pool can give a [role to a group](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-group-precedence-preferred-role), but that role reaches the app through the ID token of a signed-in user.
findings.evidence: Rule READER.md (she reads fast and must reason from what the chapter taught). User pool groups with IAM roles are never taught in 2-deep.md, and 'reaches the app through the ID token' does not say the mechanism (the identity pool reads the role from the token and only for signed-in users). Fix: 'A user pool group can name an IAM role, but the identity pool uses it only for a user who signed in; guests have no token.'
findings.resolution: q012 option c why now reads 'A user pool can give a [role to a group], but the identity pool reads that role from the token of a signed-in user, and guests have no token.' q012 is no longer shipped (exam-11).

findings.section: In one breath (hero steps); also 2-deep.md subsection 1 step 4
findings.quote: 2. IAM Identity Center opens a role in each assigned AWS account, created from a permission set.
findings.evidence: Rule STYLE one term per concept and READER.md collocations ('assume a role'). 'opens a role' and 'opens each assigned account' are not AWS collocations; the IAM chapter teaches 'assume a role' and 'a role session'. Fix: 'The employee gets a role session in each assigned AWS account, from a permission set.'
findings.resolution: Partial: 2-deep step 4 now says 'gets a role session in each assigned account'. The 1-fast hero step 2 must equal the say text of diagrams/src/identity-federation-hero.json (L703); a spec change reopens the diagrams stage, so it is left for the orchestrator.
